prompt_en: In a complex, connected photographic situation, a photographed woman is saving the last damp herbarium sheet at a wooden drying press in a botanical glasshouse after a roof leak. Her visible facial impression is guided by the supplied photograph, expressed through rounded dark eyes, softly shaped brows, a small nose and naturally glossy lips. A brief warm glance toward the camera interrupts her concentrated work. She wears a butter-yellow cotton dress with short sleeves rolled for the task; its ordinary folds follow her stance at the bench. Her left hand steadies the press edge while her right hand lays the damp paper into the open press. Both forearms stay below the visible ponytail root, keeping her work and the hairstyle legible together. Her hairstyle forms one readable arrangement on her head. Dark chestnut scalp hair converges smoothly to a single low fastening base immediately behind her right ear. One continuous loose ponytail emerges from this base, travels over her right shoulder and ends at her upper chest. A narrow three-strand scalp braid begins at her visible right temple, with its first crossing just behind the outer end of her right eyebrow. It follows the side of her head above the right ear. At least three alternating strand crossings are distinct along this temple-to-ear route. Its final crossings run along the visible outer side of the hair above and behind the upper ear rim, then slope into the upper front edge of that same low ponytail base. The whole last braided segment and its entry into the gather remain exposed on the camera-facing side, making the braid-to-root connection traceable from one crossing to the next. A deep cobalt cloth ribbon wraps this one fastening root and closes in a compact knot, two bow loops and two short ends. Immediately above the cobalt wrap, a small polished silver crescent barrette grips the gathered hair. Its lower edge meets the hair directly beside the upper edge of the wrap, and a narrow contact shadow separates rigid silver from the strands. The barrette, cloth wrap and braid terminal are neighboring parts of the same visible root assembly, while their separate materials remain readable. Rain beads cling to the glass panes; a shallow catch tray and recovered, slightly wavy herbarium papers on the bench make the recent leak and the rescue work understandable. Green leaves beyond the glass and the worn wooden press surround her without competing with the hair structure. Clear late-afternoon light after rain reveals strand crossings, cloth folds, silver edges and naturally textured skin. Photograph the scene from her front-right, about 65 degrees around toward her right side and 18 degrees above eye level. Keep environmental portrait framing, her whole head through below her waist, the entire tail and both working hands, with enough depth of field for the right temple, ear-side braid, fastening root and press to remain readable. The photograph carries a quiet, warm pause in purposeful work.
